criteria.evidence: The E1–E3 row identifies reported behavior, E4 identifies the supplied task action and successful download/open, and E5 identifies an untested report; it explicitly rejects the team’s universal editor conclusion.
It explicitly says E2 duplicates E1 and E3 repeats the same interview account, treating E1–E3 as one participant/session and E1–E4 as two participant sources without a population rate.
It retains P3’s differing account and lack of a download task, limits coverage to desktop prototype v2 on 10 October 2026, and states that prevalence and an integrated-editor need are unknown.

It keeps creation/download scope, proposes comparing P2’s input with output and clarifying P1’s changes, and tests whether correct creation details yield usable output; possible input/export causes remain unresolved and editor scope is explicitly unapproved.
The evidence table separates P1’s report, P2’s observed successful download/open and address edit, and P3’s contrasting unverified report, then rejects the team’s everybody-needs-an-editor inference.
It treats E1–E3 as one participant account and the copied note/repetition as nonindependent; the two distinct sources are correctly described as one reported account and one observed task.
It preserves E5 as contrary evidence with no verifying task, explicitly states v2/desktop/date coverage, and leaves prevalence and other devices unknown.

It recommends an in-scope intended-address creation/download comparison, observation of corrections and neutral cause inquiry, gives a disconfirming condition for its hypothesis, and requires a separate scope decision for an editor.

Its record table distinguishes P1’s reported edits from P2’s observed task and P3’s unverified contrary report; the later conclusion traces observed behavior only to P2 and rejects justification for an editor.
It identifies E1–E3 as one copied/repeated interview account, not three confirmations, and correctly identifies two distinct participants providing editing evidence without estimating frequency.
It retains P3’s account and missing download verification, opens with the specific v2 desktop date scope, and says neither user frequency nor embedded-editor need is established.

It proposes observing the existing create/download/open/check flow and investigating several possible correction causes as possibilities; a before-download correction hypothesis has a disconfirming condition, and any editor requires separate evidence and approval.

It maps E1–E3 to one reported account, E4 to an observed successful download/open followed by correction, and E5 to a contrary report without observed export success; the team’s four-confirmation interpretation is explicitly rejected.
It collapses E1–E3 to one participant/interview and correctly describes two participants providing editing evidence among three represented participants, without asserting a population rate.
It preserves E5, calls the editing signal bounded, rejects universal demand, and explicitly limits the records to v2 desktop on 10 October 2026 with mobile and population prevalence unknown.

It proposes comparing entered details with the exported address and observing a create/download/check task; missing or incorrect details are explicitly a working hypothesis with unknown cause, and persistent edits trigger a separate editor scope proposal.

The table separately identifies P1’s report, P2’s task action as described by the note, and P3’s report, while explicitly rejecting the team’s independent-confirmation and universal-editor conclusions.

It identifies E1–E3 as one participant, interview and repeated account, with no added independent confirmation; the limited editing finding correctly spans two distinct participants’ accounts/actions.
It preserves P3’s counterevidence and absent verification, limits coverage to v2 desktop on the stated date, and keeps cause and prevalence unknown rather than treating the pattern as universal.

It recommends a creation/download task comparing entered and exported addresses and neutrally asking what edits accomplish, with accurate output followed by necessary changes as counterevidence; fixes are contingent on reproduced defects and an editor remains a separate unapproved proposal.

It maps the repeated P1 report, P2’s observed successful download/open and edit, and P3’s contrary unobserved-download report to their records; it rejects universal need and the particular editor solution.
It expressly identifies E2 as duplicate and E3 as the same interview account, treating E1–E4 as two participant sources, one reported and one observed, with no population rate.
It keeps P3’s contrary account relevant without calling it verified export quality, specifies v2/desktop/date coverage, and leaves prevalence and other contexts unknown.

It proposes inspecting entered details, output and subsequent edits in the current creation/download flow, tests whether correctable creation details avoid external edits, and conditions specific in-scope fixes on findings; persistent necessary editing returns for explicit scope approval.
